comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded segment net revenue and drivers for fiscal year 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Embedded net revenue decreased by 33% to $3.6 billion in 2024 from $5.3 billion in 2023, primarily due to lower demand as customers normalized inventory levels.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address revenue drivers and customer dynamics within specific business segments, but they focus on different aspects of revenue volatility and concentration. NVIDIA highlights a material shift in fiscal 2024 where direct and indirect customers (Customer A and an indirect partner) each accounted for single-digit to high-single-digit percentages (13% and 19%) of total revenue, a change from prior years with no such concentration. In contrast, AMD's disclosure focuses on the volume decline in its Embedded segment ($3.6 billion, down 33%) driven by inventory normalization across its customer base rather than the concentration of revenue among a few major players. While NVIDIA discloses high concentration in Compute & Networking, AMD discloses a broad market-wide demand softness impacting its Embedded segment, illustrating different revenue risk profiles: specific large-customer dependency versus segment-wide volume contraction.

sentences.text: Sales to one customer, Customer A, represented 13% of total revenue for fiscal year 2024, which was attributable to the Compute & Networking segment.

One indirect customer which primarily purchases our products through system integrators and distributors, including through Customer A, is estimated to have represented approximately 19% of total revenue for fiscal year 2024, attributable to the Compute & Networking segment.
Embedded net revenue of $3.6 billion in 2024 decreased by 33%, compared to net revenue of $5.3 billion in 2023.
The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.
